title.zh: 卷三百二十 列傳第二百〇八 外國一 朝鮮
title.raw: 卷三百二十 列傳第二百〇八 外國一 朝鮮 Volume 320 Biographies 208: Foreign States 1 - Korea

sentences.zh: 朝鮮，箕子所封國也。

translations.literal: Korea was the state conferred upon Jizi.
translations.idiomatic: Korea was the state granted to Jizi as his fief.

sentences.zh: 漢以前曰朝鮮。

translations.literal: Before Han it was called Korea.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Han dynasty it was known as Korea.

sentences.zh: 始為燕人衛滿所據，漢武帝平之，置真番、臨屯、樂浪、玄菟四郡。

translations.literal: Initially it was occupied by Wei Man, a man of Yan; Emperor Wu of Han pacified it and established the four commanderies of Zhenfan, Lintun, Lelang, and Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: It was first seized by Wei Man, a refugee from Yan, and when Emperor Wu of Han conquered the region he established the four commanderies of Zhenfan, Lintun, Lelang, and Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 漢末，有扶余人高氏據其地，改國號曰高麗，又曰高句麗，居平壤，即樂浪也。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, a man of the Fuyu people surnamed Gao occupied the territory, changed the state name to Goryeo, also called Goguryeo, and dwelt at Pyongyang, which was Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Han, the Gao clan of the Fuyu people seized the region, renamed the state Goryeo—also known as Goguryeo—and made its capital at Pyongyang, formerly the seat of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 已，為唐所破，東徙。

translations.literal: Later it was defeated by Tang and moved eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Tang forces broke its power and it shifted eastward.

sentences.zh: 後唐時，王建代高氏，兼併新羅、百濟地，徙居松岳，曰東京，而以平壤為西京。

translations.literal: In Later Tang times, Wang Jian replaced the Gao clan, annexed the lands of Silla and Baekje, moved his seat to Songak, calling it the Eastern Capital, and made Pyongyang the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Tang, Wang Jian overthrew the Gao line, absorbed Silla and Baekje, moved the capital to Songak as the Eastern Capital, and retained Pyongyang as the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 其國北鄰契丹，西則女直，南曰日本，元至元中，西京內屬，置東甯路總管府，盡慈嶺為界。

translations.literal: Its state bordered the Khitan to the north, the Jurchen to the west, and Japan to the south; in the Yuan period under Zhiyuan, the Western Capital submitted and the General Administration of the Eastern Ning Circuit was established, with Jichi Ridge as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom bordered Khitan lands in the north, Jurchen territory to the west, and Japan to the south. In the Yuan reign-period Zhiyuan the Western Capital was brought under direct rule, an Eastern Ning Circuit chief commissioner's office was established, and Jichi Ridge marked the frontier.

sentences.zh: 明興，王高麗者王顓。

translations.literal: When Ming arose, the one who ruled Goryeo was Wang Zhuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming dynasty was founded, Goryeo was ruled by King Zhuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位之元年遣使賜璽書。

translations.literal: In the first year of the founding emperor's accession, envoys were dispatched bearing an imperial letter with the seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of his reign the founding emperor sent envoys bearing an imperial letter under the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 二年送還其國流人。

translations.literal: In the second year, exiles of its state were returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the court returned exiles from Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 顓表賀，貢方物，且請封。

translations.literal: Zhuan presented a memorial of congratulation, offered local products as tribute, and moreover requested investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuan sent a memorial of congratulation with tribute goods and asked to receive formal investiture.

sentences.zh: 帝遣符璽郎偰斯齎詔及金印誥文封顓為高麗國王，賜曆及錦綺。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Seal Officer Qiesi bearing an edict and golden seal patent to invest Zhuan as King of Goryeo, granting calendars and brocades.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched the seal officer Qiesi with an investiture edict, a golden seal, and patent to enfeoff Zhuan as King of Goryeo, along with calendars and brocaded silks.

sentences.zh: 其秋，顓遣總部尚書成惟得、千牛衛大將軍金甲兩上表謝，並賀天壽節，因請祭服制度，帝命工部制賜之。

translations.literal: That autumn, Zhuan sent the Director-General of the Central Secretariat Cheng Weide and the General of the Thousand-Ox Guard Jin Jialiang to present memorials of thanks, also to congratulate the Heavenly Longevity Festival, and furthermore to request regulations for sacrificial robes; the emperor ordered the Ministry of Works to manufacture and bestow them.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Zhuan sent Cheng Weide, director-general of the central secretariat, and Jin Jialiang, general of the Thousand-Ox Guard, to submit memorials of thanks and to congratulate the emperor on his birthday, while also requesting specifications for sacrificial robes; the emperor ordered the Ministry of Works to make and grant them.

sentences.zh: 惟得等辭歸，帝從容問：「王居國何為？

translations.literal: As Weide and the others took their leave to return, the emperor casually asked: What does the king do while residing in the state?
translations.idiomatic: When Weide and his party were about to depart, the emperor casually asked, "What does your king do to govern his realm?

sentences.zh: 城郭修乎？

translations.literal: Are the city walls maintained?
translations.idiomatic: Are your fortifications kept in repair?

sentences.zh: 兵甲利乎？

translations.literal: Are arms and armor sharp?
translations.idiomatic: Are your arms and armor in good order?

sentences.zh: 宮室壯乎？

translations.literal: Are the palace halls magnificent?
translations.idiomatic: Are your palaces suitably grand?

sentences.zh: 」頓首言：「東海波臣，惟知崇信釋氏，他未遑也。

translations.literal: They kowtowed and said: A wave-borne subject of the Eastern Sea knows only to revere and believe in the Buddha; he has no leisure for other matters.
translations.idiomatic: They kowtowed and answered, "Your wave-tossed subject of the Eastern Sea knows only to revere Buddhism and has had no leisure for anything else.

sentences.zh: 」遂以書諭之曰：「古者王公設險，未嘗去兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon by letter he instructed him, saying: In antiquity kings and dukes established defenses and never did away with arms.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then wrote instructing him: "In antiquity lords fortified their domains and never dispensed with arms.

sentences.zh: 民以食為天，而國必有出政令之所。

translations.literal: The people take food as Heaven, yet a state must have a place from which government orders issue.
translations.idiomatic: The people regard food as their foundation, and every state needs a place from which to issue commands.

sentences.zh: 今有人民而無城郭，人將何依？

translations.literal: Now there are people yet no city walls—where will the people rely?
translations.idiomatic: If there are subjects but no walls, what will they rely upon?

sentences.zh: 武備不修，則威弛；

translations.literal: If military preparedness is not maintained, then authority slackens.
translations.idiomatic: If military readiness is neglected, authority slackens.

sentences.zh: 地不耕，則民艱於食；

translations.literal: If the land is not cultivated, the people will struggle for food.
translations.idiomatic: If the fields go untilled, the people will lack food.

sentences.zh: 且有居室，無廳事，無以示尊嚴。

translations.literal: And though there are living quarters, there is no hall for business, and no way to display dignity.
translations.idiomatic: If there are dwellings but no hall of audience, there is no way to display royal dignity.

sentences.zh: 此數者朕甚不取。

translations.literal: In these several matters I very much disapprove.
translations.idiomatic: In all these matters I strongly disapprove.

sentences.zh: 夫國之大事，在祀與戎。

translations.literal: The great affairs of a state lie in sacrifice and war.
translations.idiomatic: The great affairs of state are sacrifice and war.

sentences.zh: 苟闕斯二者，而徒事佛求福，梁武之事，可為明鑒。

translations.literal: If these two are lacking and one merely serves the Buddha seeking blessing, the affair of Emperor Wu of Liang may serve as a clear mirror.
translations.idiomatic: To neglect both and seek blessings through Buddhism alone is a road whose end is visible in the example of Emperor Wu of Liang.

sentences.zh: 王國北接契丹、女直，而南接倭，備禦之道，王其念之。

translations.literal: Your royal state borders the Khitan and Jurchen to the north and Wa to the south; as to the way of defense and guarding, the king should bear it in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Your realm borders the Khitan and Jurchen in the north and Wa in the south; consider well how you will defend it.

sentences.zh: 」因賜之《六經》、《四書》、《通監》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted him the Six Classics, the Four Books, and the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted copies of the Six Classics, the Four Books, and the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance.

sentences.zh: 自是貢獻數至，元旦及聖節皆遣使朝賀，歲以為常。

translations.literal: From this tribute offerings came frequently; on New Year's Day and the Sacred Festival envoys were always dispatched to pay court with congratulations, and it became yearly custom.
translations.idiomatic: From then on tribute missions arrived frequently, and congratulatory envoys were sent every New Year and on the emperor's birthday as a standing practice.

sentences.zh: 三年正月命使往祀其國之山川。

translations.literal: In the third year, first month, envoys were ordered to go sacrifice to the mountains and rivers of its state.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, during the first month, the court ordered envoys to perform sacrifices to the mountains and rivers of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 是歲頒科舉詔於高麗，顓表謝，貢方物，並納元所授金印。

translations.literal: That year the civil examination edict was promulgated in Goryeo; Zhuan memorialized thanks, offered tribute goods, and also surrendered the golden seal conferred by Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: That year the civil service examination edict was promulgated in Goryeo; Zhuan sent a memorial of thanks with tribute goods and surrendered the golden seal the Yuan had conferred.

sentences.zh: 中書省言：「高麗貢使多齎私物入貨，宜徵稅；

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat said: Goryeo tribute envoys often bring private goods to sell—taxes should be levied.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Secretariat reported, "Goryeo tribute envoys often bring private goods to sell and should be taxed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又多攜中國物出境，禁之便。

translations.literal: They also often carry Chinese goods out of the realm—prohibition would be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: They also often carry goods from China out of the realm, and it would be best to forbid this.

sentences.zh: 」俱不許。

translations.literal: Both were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were rejected.

sentences.zh: 五年表請遣子弟入太學，帝曰：「入學固美事，但涉海遠，不欲者勿強。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized requesting to send sons and younger brothers to the Imperial Academy; the emperor said: Entering study is indeed a fine affair, but the sea crossing is distant—those who do not wish it should not be forced.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he memorialized asking to send sons and younger brothers to the Imperial Academy; the emperor said, "Study at court is a fine thing, but the sea voyage is long—do not force those who do not wish to go.

sentences.zh: 」貢使洪師範、鄭夢周等一百五十餘人來京，失風溺死者三十九人，師範與焉。

translations.literal: Tribute envoys Hong Shifan, Zheng Mengzhou, and more than 150 others came to the capital; thirty-nine perished in shipwreck from adverse winds, Shifan among them.
translations.idiomatic: More than 150 tribute envoys, including Hong Shifan and Zheng Mengzhou, came to the capital; thirty-nine drowned when their ships were lost in a storm, Shifan among them.

sentences.zh: 帝憫之，遣元樞密使延安答裏往諭入貢毋數。

translations.literal: The emperor took pity and sent the former Privy Council envoy Yanandali to instruct them not to send tribute so frequently.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on them and sent the former privy council envoy Yanandali to instruct Goryeo not to send tribute so often.

sentences.zh: 而顓復遣其門下贊成事姜仁裕來貢馬，其賀正旦使金湑等已先至，帝悉遣還。

translations.literal: Yet Zhuan again sent his Secretariat Associate Director Jiang Renyu to offer tribute horses; his envoys congratulating the New Year, Jin Xu and others, had already arrived first—the emperor sent them all back.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhuan again sent his secretariat associate director Jiang Renyu to offer tribute horses, while his New Year congratulatory envoys, Jin Xu and others, had already arrived; the emperor sent them all back.

sentences.zh: 謂中書省臣曰：「高麗貢獻繁數，既困敝其民，而涉海復虞覆溺。

translations.literal: He said to the Central Secretariat ministers: Goryeo's tribute offerings are excessively frequent, wearying its people, and crossing the sea again risks capsizing and drowning.
translations.idiomatic: He told the Central Secretariat ministers, "Goryeo's tribute missions are too frequent, exhausting its people, and the sea crossing again risks shipwreck and drowning.

sentences.zh: 宜遵古諸侯之禮，三年一聘。

translations.literal: It is proper to follow the rites of the ancient feudal lords—one mission every three years.
translations.idiomatic: They should follow the rites of the ancient feudal lords and send envoys once every three years.

sentences.zh: 貢物惟所產，毋過侈。

translations.literal: Tribute goods should be only what is locally produced, without excess luxury.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute goods should be limited to local products and not be excessive.

sentences.zh: 其明諭朕意。」

translations.literal: They should clearly convey my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Make my meaning clear to them."

sentences.zh: 六年，顓遣甲兩等貢馬五十匹，道亡其二，甲兩以聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Zhuan sent Jialiang and others to offer fifty horses in tribute; two were lost on the road and Jialiang reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhuan sent Jialiang and others to offer fifty horses in tribute; two were lost en route, and Jialiang reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 及進，以私馬足之。

translations.literal: When presented, he made up the count with private horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribute was presented, he made up the shortfall with his own horses.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其不誠，卻之。

translations.literal: The emperor detested his lack of sincerity and rejected them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor detested his lack of sincerity and refused the tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年遣監門護軍周誼、鄭庇等來貢，表請每歲一貢，貢道從陸，由定遼，毋涉海，其貢物稱「送太府監」。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he sent Gate Guard Army Supervisor Zhou Yi, Zheng Bi, and others to offer tribute, memorializing to request tribute once yearly by land route through Dingliao without crossing the sea, and naming the tribute goods "sent to the Directorate of Palace Provision."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he sent gate guard army supervisor Zhou Yi, Zheng Bi, and others to offer tribute, memorializing to request annual tribute by land through Dingliao without crossing the sea, and describing the goods as "sent to the Directorate of Palace Provision."

sentences.zh: 中書省言：「元時有太府監，本朝未嘗有，言涉不誠。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat said: In Yuan times there was a Directorate of Palace Provision, but this dynasty has never had one—the wording implies insincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Secretariat reported, "The Yuan had a Directorate of Palace Provision, but this dynasty has never had one—the wording suggests insincerity.

sentences.zh: 」帝命卻其貢。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the tribute rejected.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the tribute refused.

sentences.zh: 是歲顓為權相李仁人所弑。

translations.literal: That year Zhuan was assassinated by the powerful minister Li Renren.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhuan was assassinated by the powerful minister Li Renren.

sentences.zh: 顓無子，以寵臣辛肫之子禑為子，於是仁人立禑。

translations.literal: Zhuan had no son and had taken Sin Chun's son Bong as his son; thereupon Renren enthroned Bong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuan had no son of his own and had adopted Bong, son of his favored minister Sin Chun; Renren thereupon enthroned Bong.

sentences.zh: 八年，禑遣判宗簿事崔原來告哀，且言前有貢使金義殺朝使蔡斌，今嗣王禑已誅義，籍其家。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Bong sent Director of the Register of the Ancestral Temple Cui Yuan to announce mourning, and moreover stated that formerly the tribute envoy Jin Yi had killed the dynastic envoy Cai Bin, but now the succeeding king Bong had executed Yi and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Bong sent director of the register of the ancestral temple Cui Yuan to announce mourning, reporting that the former tribute envoy Jin Yi had killed the Ming envoy Cai Bin and that the succeeding king Bong had now executed Yi and confiscated his property.

sentences.zh: 帝疑其詐，拘原而遣使往祭吊。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected deception, detained Yuan, and sent envoys to perform sacrificial rites of condolence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected deception, detained Yuan, and sent envoys to perform sacrificial rites of condolence.

sentences.zh: 十年，使來請故王顓諡號，帝曰：「顓被殺已久，今始請諡，將假吾朝命，鎮撫其民，且掩其弑逆之跡，不可許。

translations.literal: In the tenth year envoys came requesting the posthumous title of the former king Zhuan; the emperor said: Zhuan was killed long ago—now they first request a posthumous title, intending to borrow our dynasty's authority to pacify their people and cover the traces of regicide—it cannot be granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year envoys came requesting a posthumous title for the former king Zhuan; the emperor said, "Zhuan was killed long ago, and they now ask for a posthumous title only to borrow our authority to pacify their people and cover the traces of regicide—it cannot be granted.

sentences.zh: 前所留使者，其遣之。

translations.literal: The envoys previously detained should be sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Send back the envoys previously detained.

sentences.zh: 」於是釋原歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuan was released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was then released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 其夏，復遣周誼貢馬及方物，卻不受。

translations.literal: That summer he again sent Zhou Yi to offer horses and local products—they were refused and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he again sent Zhou Yi with horses and local products, but the tribute was refused.

sentences.zh: 冬，又遣使賀明年正旦。

translations.literal: In winter envoys were again sent to congratulate the New Year of the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: In winter envoys were again sent to congratulate the New Year of the coming year.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「高麗王顓被弑，奸臣竊命，《春秋》之義，亂臣必誅，夫又何言。

translations.literal: The emperor said: King Zhuan of Goryeo was assassinated and treacherous ministers usurped authority—in the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, rebellious ministers must be punished; what more is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "King Zhuan of Goryeo was assassinated and treacherous ministers usurped power—in the sense of the Spring and Autumn Annals, rebellious ministers must be punished; what more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 第前後使者皆稱嗣王所遣，中書宜遣人往問嗣王如何，政令安在。

translations.literal: Only that envoys before and after all say they were dispatched by the succeeding king—the Central Secretariat should send someone to inquire how the succeeding king is and where governmental orders lie.
translations.idiomatic: Yet envoys before and after all claim to have been sent by the succeeding king; the Central Secretariat should send someone to inquire into the succeeding king's condition and where governmental authority now lies.

sentences.zh: 若政令如前，嗣王不為羈囚，則當依前王言，歲貢馬千匹，明年貢金百斤、銀萬兩、良馬百、細布萬，仍悉送還所拘遼東民，方見王位真而政令行，朕無惑已。

translations.literal: If governmental orders proceed as before and the succeeding king is not a captive prisoner, then according to the former king's words he should yearly offer a thousand horses, and next year offer a hundred catties of gold, ten thousand taels of silver, a hundred fine horses, and ten thousand bolts of fine cloth, and furthermore fully return the Liaodong people detained—only then will it be seen that the kingship is genuine and orders are enforced, and I shall no longer be in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: If governmental orders proceed as before and the succeeding king is not a captive, then according to the former king's words he should yearly offer a thousand horses, and next year offer a hundred catties of gold, ten thousand taels of silver, a hundred fine horses, and ten thousand bolts of fine cloth, while fully returning all Liaodong people detained—only then will it be clear that the kingship is genuine and orders are enforced, and I shall no longer be in doubt.

sentences.zh: 否則弑君之賊，必討無赦。」

translations.literal: Otherwise the regicide villains must be punished without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the regicides must be punished without pardon."

sentences.zh: 十一年四月，禑復命誼來貢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, fourth month, Bong again ordered Yi to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, fourth month, Bong again ordered Yi to come with tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二年敕遼東守將潘敬、葉旺等謹飭邊備。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the frontier commanders of Liaodong Pan Jing, Ye Wang, and others were ordered to carefully maintain border defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Liaodong frontier commanders Pan Jing, Ye Wang, and others were ordered to tighten border defenses.

sentences.zh: 其冬，禑遣李茂芳等來貢，以不如約卻之。

translations.literal: That winter Bong sent Li Maofang and others to offer tribute—they were rejected for failing to fulfill the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Bong sent Li Maofang and others with tribute, but it was rejected because they had not fulfilled the agreement.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遼東送高麗使誼至京師，帝敕敬等曰：「高麗弑君，又殺朝使，前堅請入貢又不如期，今遣誼來，以虛文飾詐，他日必為邊患。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Liaodong escorted the Goryeo envoy Yi to the capital; the emperor instructed Jing and others: Goryeo regicides also killed our envoys; they previously insisted on offering tribute yet again failed to meet the deadline—now sending Yi with empty words to gloss over deception, they will surely become a frontier trouble one day.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Liaodong escorted the Goryeo envoy Yi to the capital; the emperor instructed Jing and others, "Goryeo's regicides also killed our envoys; they insisted on offering tribute yet again failed to meet the deadline—now sending Yi with empty words to gloss over deception, they will surely become a frontier threat.

sentences.zh: 自今來者，其絕勿通。

translations.literal: From now on, whoever comes should be cut off and not admitted.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, cut off all who come and do not admit them.

sentences.zh: 」因留誼于京師。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi was detained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was therefore detained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 十六年來貢，卻之，命禮部責其朝貢過期、陪臣侮慢之罪；

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year they came with tribute—it was refused; the Ministry of Rites was ordered to charge them with the offenses of overdue tribute and disrespect by accompanying ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year they came with tribute and it was refused; the Ministry of Rites was ordered to charge them with overdue tribute and disrespect by accompanying ministers.

sentences.zh: 誠欲聽約者，當以前五歲違約不貢之物並至。

translations.literal: If they truly wish to abide by the agreement, the goods owed from the previous five years of breached tribute should all be delivered together.
translations.idiomatic: If they truly wish to abide by the agreement, they must deliver together all goods owed from the previous five years of breached tribute.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月，禑遣司僕正崔涓、禮儀判書金進宜貢馬二千匹。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, sixth month, Bong sent Master of the Stud Cui Juan and Director of Ritual Protocol Jin Jinyi to offer two thousand horses in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, sixth month, Bong sent master of the stud Cui Juan and director of ritual protocol Jin Jinyi to offer two thousand horses in tribute.

sentences.zh: 且言金非地所產，願以馬代輸，餘皆如約。

translations.literal: Moreover stating that gold was not produced locally, they wished to substitute horses in payment—all else according to the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: They also reported that gold was not produced locally and asked to substitute horses in payment, with all else according to the agreement.

sentences.zh: 遼東守將唐勝宗為之請，帝許之。

translations.literal: The Liaodong frontier commander Tang Shengzhong pleaded on their behalf and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong frontier commander Tang Shengzhong pleaded on their behalf, and the emperor granted the request.

sentences.zh: 然請顓諡號，襲王爵，未允也。

translations.literal: However the requests for Zhuan's posthumous title and succession to the kingship were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: However, the requests for Zhuan's posthumous title and succession to the kingship were not granted.

sentences.zh: 十八年正月，貢使至。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, first month, the tribute envoys arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, first month, the tribute envoys arrived.

sentences.zh: 帝諭禮臣曰：「高麗屢請約束，朕數不允，而其請不已，故索歲貢以試其誠偽，非以此為富也。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the rites officials: Goryeo repeatedly requests binding agreements—I have several times not granted them, yet their requests never cease—therefore I demanded yearly tribute to test their sincerity or deception, not to enrich myself thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed the rites officials, "Goryeo has repeatedly requested binding agreements; I have several times refused, yet their requests never cease—therefore I demanded yearly tribute to test their sincerity, not to enrich myself.

sentences.zh: 今既聽命，宜損其貢數，令三年一朝，貢馬五十匹。

translations.literal: Now that they have obeyed, the tribute quota should be reduced—let them come once every three years and offer fifty horses.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they have obeyed, their tribute quota should be reduced: let them come once every three years and offer fifty horses.

sentences.zh: 至二十一年正旦乃貢。

translations.literal: The tribute should be offered only at the New Year of the twenty-first year.
translations.idiomatic: The next tribute should be offered at the New Year of the twenty-first year.

sentences.zh: 」七月，禑上表請襲爵，並請故王諡。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Bong submitted a memorial requesting succession to the title and also requesting a posthumous title for the former king.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Bong submitted a memorial requesting succession to the kingship and a posthumous title for the former king.

sentences.zh: 命封禑為高麗國王，賜故王顓諡恭湣。

translations.literal: He was ordered enfeoffed as King of Goryeo and the former king Zhuan was granted the posthumous title Gongmin.
translations.idiomatic: Bong was enfeoffed as King of Goryeo, and the former king Zhuan was granted the posthumous title Gongmin.

sentences.zh: 十九年二月遣使貢布萬匹、馬千匹。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, second month, envoys were dispatched offering ten thousand bolts of cloth and a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, second month, envoys were sent offering ten thousand bolts of cloth and a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 九月，表賀，貢方物。

translations.literal: In the ninth month memorials of congratulation were sent with tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month congratulatory memorials were sent with tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 其後貢獻輒逾常額，且未嘗至三年也。

translations.literal: Thereafter tribute offerings repeatedly exceeded the regular quota, and the three-year interval was never observed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute repeatedly exceeded the regular quota, and the three-year interval was never observed.

sentences.zh: 冬，詔遣指揮僉事高家奴以綺布市馬於高麗。

translations.literal: In winter an edict dispatched Assistant Commander Gao Jianu to purchase horses in Goryeo with brocades and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: In winter an edict dispatched assistant commander Gao Jianu to purchase horses in Goryeo with brocades and cloth.

sentences.zh: 二十年三月，高家奴還，陳高麗表辭馬直，帝敕如數償之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, third month, Gao Jianu returned and reported Goryeo's memorial declining horse prices—the emperor ordered payment in full according to the count.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, third month, Gao Jianu returned and reported Goryeo's memorial declining payment for the horses; the emperor ordered full payment according to the count.

sentences.zh: 先是，元末遼、瀋兵起，民避亂，轉徙高麗。

translations.literal: Earlier, when military disturbances arose in Liaoning and Shenyang at the end of Yuan, people fleeing turmoil migrated to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when military disturbances arose in Liaoning and Shenyang at the end of the Yuan, people fleeing the turmoil migrated to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 至是因市馬，帝令就索之，遂以遼、瀋流民三百餘口來歸。

translations.literal: At this time, because of the horse purchase, the emperor ordered them sought there—thereupon more than three hundred exiles from Liaoning and Shenyang returned.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion, because of the horse purchase, the emperor ordered them sought out there, and more than three hundred exiles from Liaoning and Shenyang returned.

sentences.zh: 十二月命戶部咨高麗王：「鐵嶺北，東西之地，舊屬開元者，遼東統之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to inform the King of Goryeo: North of Tie Ridge, the lands east and west that formerly belonged to Kaiyuan shall be governed by Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to inform the King of Goryeo, "North of Tie Ridge, the lands east and west that formerly belonged to Kaiyuan shall be governed by Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 鐵嶺之南，舊屬高麗者，本國統之。

translations.literal: South of Tie Ridge, what formerly belonged to Goryeo shall be governed by your state.
translations.idiomatic: South of Tie Ridge, what formerly belonged to Goryeo shall be governed by your state.

sentences.zh: 各正疆境，毋侵越。」

translations.literal: Each should rectify the border and not encroach.
translations.idiomatic: Each side should rectify its borders and not encroach."

sentences.zh: 二十一年四月，禑表言，鐵嶺之地實其世守，乞仍舊便。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, fourth month, Bong memorialized saying the Tie Ridge region was in fact held by his house for generations and requested it remain as before for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, fourth month, Bong memorialized that the Tie Ridge region had in fact been held by his house for generations and asked that it remain as before.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「高麗舊以鴨綠江為界，今飾辭鐵嶺，詐偽昭然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: Goryeo formerly took the Yalu River as boundary—now dressing up words about Tie Ridge, deception is manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Goryeo formerly took the Yalu River as its boundary; now dressing up words about Tie Ridge, its deception is manifest.

sentences.zh: 其以朕言諭之，俾安分，毋生釁端。

translations.literal: Let my words be conveyed to them, that they keep to their place and not create incidents.
translations.idiomatic: Convey my words to them, that they keep to their place and not create incidents.

sentences.zh: 」八月，高麗千戶陳景來降，言：「是年四月，禑欲寇遼東，使都軍相崔瑩、李成桂繕兵西京。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Goryeo chiliarch Chen Jing came over in surrender, stating: That year in the fourth month Bong wished to raid Liaodong and ordered the commander-in-chief Cui Ying and Li Chenggui to ready troops at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Goryeo chiliarch Chen Jing defected, reporting, "That year in the fourth month Bong intended to raid Liaodong and ordered commander-in-chief Cui Ying and Li Chenggui to ready troops at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 成桂使陳景屯艾州，以糧不繼退師。

translations.literal: Chenggui sent Chen Jing to garrison Aizhou; because supplies did not continue the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggui sent Chen Jing to garrison Aizhou, but because supplies failed the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 王怒，殺成桂之子。

translations.literal: The king in anger killed Chenggui's son.
translations.idiomatic: The king in anger killed Chenggui's son.

sentences.zh: 成桂還兵攻破王城，囚王及瑩。

translations.literal: Chenggui turned his army back, stormed the royal city, and imprisoned the king and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggui turned his army back, stormed the royal city, and imprisoned the king and Ying.

sentences.zh: 」景懼及，故降。

translations.literal: Chen feared he would be implicated, therefore he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would be implicated, Chen surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝敕遼東嚴守備，仍遣人偵之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Liaodong to strictly maintain defenses and still sent men to reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Liaodong to tighten its defenses and sent men to reconnoiter.

sentences.zh: 十月，禑請遜位於其子昌。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Bong requested to abdicate in favor of his son Chang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Bong requested to abdicate in favor of his son Chang.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「前聞其王被囚，此必成桂之謀，姑俟之以觀變。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: Earlier we heard their king was imprisoned—this must be Chenggui's plot; for the moment let us wait and observe how affairs change.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "We earlier heard that their king had been imprisoned—this must surely be Chenggui's doing; let us wait for now and see how affairs develop."

sentences.zh: 二十二年，權國事昌奏乞入朝，帝不許。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, regent Chang memorialized requesting to come to court; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, regent Chang memorialized requesting an audience at court, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 是歲，成桂廢昌，而立定昌國院君瑤。

translations.literal: That year Chenggui deposed Chang and enthroned Lord of Jeongchang State Academy Yao.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chenggui deposed Chang and installed Jeongchang Academy Lord Yao as ruler.

sentences.zh: 二十三年正月遣使來告。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, first month, envoys were dispatched to come and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, first month, envoys were sent to report the change.

sentences.zh: 二十四年三月詔市馬高麗。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, third month, an edict ordered horse purchases in Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, third month, an edict ordered the purchase of horses in Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 八月，權國事瑤進所市馬千五百匹。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, regent Yao presented one thousand five hundred horses from the purchased stock.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, regent Yao presented fifteen hundred horses purchased under the edict.

sentences.zh: 帝曰；

translations.literal: The emperor said;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said;

sentences.zh: 「三韓君臣悖亂，二紀於茲。

translations.literal: The ministers and ruler of the Three Han have been rebellious and disorderly—for two reign-periods now.
translations.idiomatic: "For two reign-periods now, the rulers and ministers of the Three Han have been in rebellion and disorder.

sentences.zh: 今王瑤嗣立，乃王氏苗裔，宜遣使勞之。

translations.literal: Now King Yao has succeeded to the throne; he is a scion of the Wang house—it is fitting to dispatch envoys to console him.
translations.idiomatic: King Yao has now succeeded to the throne; he is a descendant of the Wang house, and envoys should be sent to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，瑤遣其子奭朝賀明年正旦。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Yao sent his son Suk to court to congratulate the New Year's Day of the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: "In the twelfth month Yao sent his son Suk to court to congratulate the New Year of the coming year.

sentences.zh: 奭未歸而成桂自立，遂有其國，瑤出居原州。

translations.literal: Before Suk returned Chenggui established himself and seized the state; Yao went out to dwell at Wonju.
translations.idiomatic: Before Suk returned, Chenggui declared himself ruler and took possession of the kingdom; Yao withdrew to Wonju.

sentences.zh: 王氏自五代傳國數百年，至是絕。

translations.literal: The Wang house had transmitted the state for several hundred years since the Five Dynasties period—at this point it ended.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang house had held the throne for several hundred years since the Five Dynasties period; with this it came to an end.

sentences.zh: 二十五年九月，高麗知密直司事趙胖等持國都評議司奏言：「本國自恭湣王薨，無嗣，權臣李仁人以辛肫子禑主國事，昏暴好殺，至欲興師犯邊，大將李成桂以為不可而回軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, ninth month, Goryeo Secret Affairs Director Zhao Pang and others presented a memorial from the State Capital Deliberative Office, stating: Since King Gongmin of our state died without an heir, the powerful minister Li Renren installed Sin Chun's son Bong to manage state affairs; he was dim-witted, violent, and fond of killing—to the point of wishing to raise troops and violate the border; the grand general Li Chenggui held this impossible and turned the army back.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, ninth month, Goryeo secret affairs director Zhao Pang and others presented a memorial from the state capital deliberative office, stating, "Since King Gongmin of our state died without an heir, the powerful minister Li Renren installed Sin Chun's son Bong to manage state affairs. He was tyrannical and bloodthirsty, even wishing to raise troops and violate the frontier; grand general Li Chenggui deemed this impossible and turned the army back.

sentences.zh: 禑負罪惶懼，遜位於子昌。

translations.literal: Bong, burdened with guilt and fearful, abdicated in favor of his son Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Burdened with guilt and fear, Bong abdicated in favor of his son Chang.

sentences.zh: 國人弗順，啟請恭湣王妃安氏擇宗親瑤權國事。

translations.literal: The people did not acquiesce; they petitioned Queen Consort An of King Gongmin to select a clansman Yao to manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The people would not accept this and petitioned Queen Consort An, widow of King Gongmin, to select the clansman Yao to manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 已及四年，昏戾信讒，戕害勳舊，子奭癡騃不慧，國人謂瑤不足主社稷。

translations.literal: More than four years had passed; he was dim, perverse, and believed slanders, slaying meritorious elders; his son Suk was dull and feeble-minded, and the people considered Yao unfit to hold the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Four years had passed; he was muddled and perverse, believed slanders, and killed meritorious elders; his son Suk was dull and simple-minded, and the people deemed Yao unfit to rule the state.

sentences.zh: 今以安氏命，退瑤於私第。

translations.literal: Now by Queen An's command Yao has been retired to a private residence.
translations.idiomatic: By Queen An's command Yao has now been retired to a private residence.

sentences.zh: 王氏子姓無可當輿望者，中外人心咸系成桂。

translations.literal: Among Wang clansmen there is none who can bear the hopes of the people; within and without, all hearts are fixed on Chenggui.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Wang clansmen there is none who can command public confidence; inside and outside the court, all hearts turn to Chenggui.

sentences.zh: 臣等與國人耆老共推主國事，惟聖主俞允。

translations.literal: We ministers together with the elders of the state jointly recommend him to manage state affairs—may the sage sovereign graciously assent.
translations.idiomatic: We ministers, together with the elders of the state, jointly recommend him to manage state affairs, and ask that the sage sovereign graciously assent.

sentences.zh: 」帝以高麗僻處東隅，非中國所治，令禮部移諭：「果能順天道，合人心，不啟邊釁，使命往來，實爾國之福，我又何誅。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that Goryeo lies remote in the eastern corner and is not territory that China governs, ordered the Ministry of Rites to transmit instructions: If you can indeed follow Heaven's Way, accord with the people's hearts, and not provoke border incidents, then the coming and going of missions will truly be your state's blessing—why should I punish you?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, considering that Goryeo lay remote in the eastern corner and was not territory under China's direct governance, ordered the Ministry of Rites to transmit instructions: "If you can indeed follow Heaven's way, accord with the people's hearts, and not provoke border incidents, then the exchange of missions will truly be your state's blessing—why should I punish you?

sentences.zh: 」冬，成桂聞皇太子薨，遣使表慰，並請更國號。

translations.literal: In winter Chenggui, hearing that the crown prince had died, dispatched envoys with a memorial of condolence and also requested to change the state name.
translations.idiomatic: "In winter Chenggui, hearing that the crown prince had died, dispatched envoys with a memorial of condolence and also requested to change the state name.

sentences.zh: 帝命仍古號曰朝鮮。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that the ancient name Korea be retained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that the ancient name Korea be retained.

sentences.zh: 二十六年二月遣使進馬九千八百餘匹，命運糸寧絲綿布一萬九千七百餘匹酬之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, second month, envoys were dispatched presenting more than nine thousand eight hundred horses; the court ordered shipment of more than nineteen thousand seven hundred bolts of silk, floss silk, and cotton cloth in payment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, second month, envoys were sent presenting more than nine thousand eight hundred horses; the court ordered more than nineteen thousand seven hundred bolts of silk, floss silk, and cotton cloth shipped in payment.

sentences.zh: 六月表謝，貢馬及方物，並上前恭湣王金印，請更己名曰旦。

translations.literal: In the sixth month a memorial of thanks was sent, with tribute horses and local products, and also surrender of the former King Gongmin's golden seal; he requested to change his personal name to Dan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month a memorial of thanks was sent with tribute horses and local products, and the former King Gongmin's golden seal was surrendered; he requested to change his personal name to Dan.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 是月，遼東都指揮使司奏，朝鮮國招引女直五百餘人，潛渡鴨綠江，欲入寇。

translations.literal: That month the Liaodong Regional Military Commission memorialized that the state of Korea had recruited more than five hundred Jurchen, secretly crossed the Yalu River, and intended to raid.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Liaodong regional military commission reported that Korea had recruited more than five hundred Jurchen, secretly crossed the Yalu River, and intended to raid.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使敕諭，示以禍福。

translations.literal: Thereupon envoys were dispatched with an imperial instruction, showing them fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were then dispatched with an imperial instruction, showing them the consequences of fortune and disaster.

sentences.zh: 旦得敕，惶懼陳謝，上貢，並械送逋逃軍民三百八十餘人至遼東。

translations.literal: Dan received the instruction, in fear and trepidation presented an apology, sent tribute, and also sent under guard more than three hundred eighty deserting soldiers and civilians to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Dan received the instruction, and in fear and trepidation presented an apology, sent tribute, and also sent more than three hundred eighty deserting soldiers and civilians under guard to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，旦遣子入貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Dan sent his son to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Dan sent his son to offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十八年遣使柳珣賀明年正旦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the envoy Liu Xun was dispatched to congratulate the New Year of the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year the envoy Liu Xun was dispatched to congratulate the New Year of the coming year.

sentences.zh: 帝以表文語慢，詰責之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the memorial's language was disrespectful, reprimanded and censured him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding the memorial's language disrespectful, reprimanded and censured him.

sentences.zh: 珣言表文乃門下評理鄭道傳所撰，遂命逮道傳，釋珣歸。

translations.literal: Xun stated that the memorial had been composed by Secretariat Assessor Zheng Daotong; thereupon the court ordered Daotong arrested and released Xun to return.
translations.idiomatic: Xun stated that the memorial had been composed by secretariat assessor Zheng Daotong; the court then ordered Daotong arrested and released Xun to return.

sentences.zh: 二十九年送撰表人鄭總等三人至，雲表實總等所撰，道傳病不能行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year they sent the memorial-drafters Zheng Zong and two others; it was said the memorial had in fact been written by Zong and the others, and Daotong was ill and could not travel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year they sent the memorial-drafters Zheng Zong and two others; they said the memorial had in fact been written by Zong and the others, and that Daotong was too ill to travel.

sentences.zh: 帝以總等亂邦構釁，留不遣。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that Zong and the others had disordered the state and provoked border incidents, detained them and did not send them back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, holding that Zong and the others had disordered the state and provoked border incidents, detained them and did not send them back.

sentences.zh: 三十年冬，復以表涉譏訕，拘其使。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, winter, again because the memorial involved ridicule and satire, his envoy was detained.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, winter, again because the memorial involved ridicule and satire, the envoy was detained.

sentences.zh: 建文初，旦表陳年老，以子芳遠襲位。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign, Dan memorialized stating he was old in years and had his son Fangyuan succeed to the position.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign, Dan memorialized that he was advanced in years and had his son Bang-won (Fangyuan) succeed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 成祖立，遣官頒即位詔。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor established himself, officials were dispatched to promulgate the accession edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor established himself, officials were dispatched to promulgate the accession edict.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年正月，芳遠遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, first month, Fangyuan dispatched envoys to pay court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongle, first month, Bang-won dispatched envoys to pay court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 四月復遣陪臣李貴齡入貢，奏芳遠父有疾，需龍腦、沈香、蘇合、香油諸物，齎布求市。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he again sent attending minister Li Guiling to offer tribute, memorializing that Fangyuan's father was ill and needed dragon's brain, aloeswood, storax, sesame oil, and other items, bringing cloth to request purchase.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he again sent attending minister Li Guiling to offer tribute, reporting that Bang-won's father was ill and needed dragon's brain, aloeswood, storax, sesame oil, and other items, and brought cloth to request purchase.

sentences.zh: 帝命太醫院賜之，還其布。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Imperial Medical Academy to bestow them and returned his cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Imperial Medical Academy to bestow them and returned his cloth.

sentences.zh: 芳遠表謝，因請冕服書藉。

translations.literal: Fangyuan sent a memorial of thanks and moreover requested court robes and books.
translations.idiomatic: Bang-won sent a memorial of thanks and also requested court robes and books.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其能慕中國禮，賜金印、誥命、冕服、九章、圭玉、珮玉，妃珠翠七翟冠、霞帔、金墜，及經籍彩幣表裏。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his ability to admire Chinese rites and granted a golden seal, patent of appointment, court robes, nine insignia, jade scepter, pendant jade, for the consort a pearl-and-kingfisher-feather seven-pheasant crown, embroidered cape, gold pendants, and classics, silk brocades for outer and inner garments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his admiration for Chinese rites and granted a golden seal, patent of appointment, court robes, nine insignia, a jade scepter and pendant jade, for the consort a pearl-and-kingfisher seven-pheasant crown, embroidered cape, and gold pendants, as well as classics and brocades for outer and inner garments.

sentences.zh: 自後貢獻，歲輒四五至焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter tribute offerings came four or five times each year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute missions came four or five times each year.

sentences.zh: 二年十二月詔立芳遠子禔為世子，從其請也。

translations.literal: In the second year, twelfth month, an edict established Fangyuan's son Je as heir apparent—acceding to his request.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, twelfth month, an edict established Bang-won's son Je as heir apparent, acceding to his request.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月，貢馬三千匹至遼東，命戶部運絹布萬五千匹償之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, twelfth month, three thousand tribute horses arrived at Liaodong; the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to transport ten thousand five hundred bolts of silk cloth in payment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, twelfth month, three thousand tribute horses arrived at Liaodong; the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to transport ten thousand five hundred bolts of silk cloth in payment.

sentences.zh: 六年，世子禔來朝，賜織金文綺。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the heir apparent Je came to court and was granted gold-woven brocades.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year heir apparent Je came to court and was granted gold-woven brocades.

sentences.zh: 及歸，帝親制詩賜之。

translations.literal: When he returned the emperor personally composed a poem and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, the emperor personally composed a poem and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 時朝鮮納女後宮，立為妃嬪者四人。

translations.literal: At that time Korea offered women to the inner palace; four were established as consorts and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Korea offered women to the inner palace, and four were established as consorts and concubines.

sentences.zh: 其秋，遣陪臣鄭擢來告其父旦之喪。

translations.literal: That autumn he sent attending minister Zheng Zhuo to report the death of his father Dan.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he sent attending minister Zheng Zhuo to report the death of his father Dan.

sentences.zh: 命官弔祭，賜諡康獻。

translations.literal: Officials were ordered to offer condolences and sacrifices; the posthumous title Kangxian was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were ordered to offer condolences and sacrifices, and the posthumous title Kangxian was granted.

sentences.zh: 十六年奏世子禔不肖，第三子祹孝弟力學，國人所屬，請立為嗣，詔聽王所擇。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he memorialized that heir apparent Je was unworthy, while the third son Do was filial, fraternal, and diligent in learning—the people looked to him—and requested he be established as successor; an edict granted the king his choice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he memorialized that heir apparent Je was unworthy, while the third son Do was filial, fraternal, and diligent in learning—the people looked to him—and requested that he be established as successor; an edict granted the king his choice.

sentences.zh: 因上表謝，並陳己年老，請以祹理國事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he presented a memorial of thanks and also stated he was old in years, requesting that Do manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented a memorial of thanks and also stated that he was advanced in years, requesting that Do manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 命光祿少卿韓確、鴻臚丞劉泉封祹為朝鮮國王。

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Han Que and Honglu Secretariat Assistant Liu Quan were ordered to invest Do as King of Korea.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Han Que and Honglu secretariat assistant Liu Quan were ordered to invest Do as King of Korea.

sentences.zh: 時帝已遷北都，朝鮮益近，而事大之禮益恭，朝廷亦待以加禮，他國不敢望也。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had already moved the capital north; Korea was all the nearer, and its rites of serving the great power grew ever more deferential—the court also treated it with added ceremony, which other states did not dare expect.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had already moved the capital north; Korea was all the nearer, and its rites of serving the great power grew ever more deferential—the court also treated it with added ceremony, which other states did not dare expect.

sentences.zh: 二十年，芳遠卒，賜諡恭定。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Fangyuan died; the posthumous title Gongding was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Bang-won died, and the posthumous title Gongding was granted.

sentences.zh: 二十一年七月，祹請立嫡子珦為世子，從之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, seventh month, Do requested to establish his eldest son Gyeong as heir apparent; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, seventh month, Do requested to establish his eldest son Gyeong as heir apparent, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 先是，敕祹貢馬萬匹，至是如數至，賜白金綺絹。

translations.literal: Earlier an instruction had ordered Do to offer ten thousand horses in tribute; by this time the full number had arrived and white silver and brocade silk were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an instruction had ordered Do to offer ten thousand horses in tribute; by this time the full number had arrived, and white silver and brocade silk were granted.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年三月遣中官賜白金糸寧紗，別敕進馬五千匹，資邊用。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande, third month, palace eunuchs were dispatched to grant white silver and silk gauze; a separate instruction ordered the presentation of five thousand horses to supply the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande, third month, palace eunuchs were dispatched to grant white silver and silk gauze; a separate instruction ordered the presentation of five thousand horses to supply the border.

sentences.zh: 九月如數至。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the full number arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the full number arrived.

sentences.zh: 四年祹賜書：「珍禽異獸，非朕所貴，其勿獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Do was granted a letter: Rare birds and exotic beasts are not what I value—do not present them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Do was granted a letter: "Rare birds and exotic beasts are not what I value—do not present them.

sentences.zh: 」後又敕祹：「金玉之器，非爾國所產，宜止之，土物效誠而已。

translations.literal: Later another instruction to Do: Vessels of gold and jade are not products of your state—you should cease them; local goods to show sincerity are enough.
translations.idiomatic: "Later another instruction to Do: "Vessels of gold and jade are not products of your state—you should cease presenting them; local goods to show sincerity are enough.

sentences.zh: 」八年，祹奏遣子弟詣太學或遼東學，帝不許，賜《五經》、《四書》、《性理》、《通鑒綱目》諸書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Do memorialized requesting to send sons and younger brothers to the Imperial Academy or the Liaodong Academy; the emperor did not permit it but granted the Five Classics, Four Books, Xingli, and Zizhi Tongjian Gangmu and other books.
translations.idiomatic: "In the eighth year Do memorialized requesting to send sons and younger brothers to the Imperial Academy or the Liaodong Academy; the emperor did not permit it but granted the Five Classics, Four Books, Xingli, Zizhi Tongjian Gangmu, and other books.

sentences.zh: 正統元年三月放朝鮮婦女金黑等五十三人還其國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong, third month, fifty-three Korean women including Jin Hei were released and sent back to their state.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengtong, third month, fifty-three Korean women including Jin Hei were released and sent back to their state.

sentences.zh: 金黑等自宣德初至京師，至是遣中官送回。

translations.literal: Jin Hei and the others had come to the capital since the beginning of Xuande; on this occasion palace eunuchs were dispatched to escort them back.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Hei and the others had come to the capital since the beginning of Xuande; on this occasion palace eunuchs were dispatched to escort them back.

sentences.zh: 三年八月賜祹遠遊冠、絳紗袍、玉佩、赤舄。

translations.literal: In the third year, eighth month, Do was granted the distant-travel crown, crimson gauze robe, jade pendant, and red slippers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, eighth month, Do was granted the distant-travel crown, crimson gauze robe, jade pendant, and red slippers.

sentences.zh: 先是，建州長童倉避居朝鮮界，已復還建州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jianzhou chieftain Tongcang had taken refuge within Korea's border and had already returned to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jianzhou chieftain Tongcang had taken refuge within Korea's border and had already returned to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮言：「昔以窮歸臣，臣遇之善。

translations.literal: Korea stated: Formerly he came in destitution to submit to us; we treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Korea stated, "Formerly he came in destitution to submit to us, and we treated him well.

sentences.zh: 今負恩還建州李滿住所，慮其同謀擾邊。

translations.literal: Now ungratefully he has returned to Li Manju's place in Jianzhou—we fear they will conspire together to disturb the border.
translations.idiomatic: Now, ungratefully, he has returned to Li Manju's place in Jianzhou, and we fear they will conspire together to disturb the border.

sentences.zh: 」建州長言，所部為朝鮮追殺，阻留一百七十餘家。

translations.literal: The Jianzhou chieftain stated that his followers had been pursued and killed by Korea, and more than one hundred seventy households were blocked and detained.
translations.idiomatic: "The Jianzhou chieftain stated that his followers had been pursued and killed by Korea, and more than one hundred seventy households were blocked and detained.

sentences.zh: 五年詔祹還之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict ordered Do to return them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict ordered Do to return them.

sentences.zh: 七年五月諭祹曰：「鴨綠江一帶東甯等衛，密邇王境，中多細人逃至王國，或被國人誘脅去者，無問漢人、女直，至即解京。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, fifth month, Do was instructed: Along the Yalu River the guards such as Eastern Ning closely border your realm; among them many common folk flee to your kingdom, or are lured and coerced away by your people—regardless of whether Han Chinese or Jurchen, when they arrive send them immediately to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, fifth month, Do was instructed, "Along the Yalu River the guards such as Eastern Ning closely border your realm; among them many common folk flee to your kingdom, or are lured and coerced away by your people—regardless of whether Han Chinese or Jurchen, when they arrive send them immediately to the capital.

sentences.zh: 」初，瓦剌密令女直諸部誘朝鮮，使背中國。

translations.literal: Earlier the Oirats secretly ordered the Jurchen tribes to entice Korea, making it turn against China.
translations.idiomatic: "Earlier the Oirats secretly ordered the Jurchen tribes to entice Korea, making it turn against China.

sentences.zh: 祹拒之，白其事於朝。

translations.literal: Do refused them and reported the matter to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Do refused them and reported the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其忠，敕獎之，並賜彩幣。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his loyalty, issued an instruction praising him, and also granted colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his loyalty, issued an instruction praising him, and also granted colored silks.

sentences.zh: 九年春，倭寇犯邊，祹命將擒獲五十餘人，械送京師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, spring, Wa pirates violated the border; Do ordered his generals to capture more than fifty men and sent them in bonds to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, spring, Wa pirates violated the border; Do ordered his generals to capture more than fifty men and sent them in bonds to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十年又獲餘黨來獻。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the remaining band was again captured and presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the remaining band was again captured and presented.

sentences.zh: 帝連敕獎諭，賜賚加等。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly issued instructions praising and instructing him, with enhanced gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly issued instructions praising and instructing him, with enhanced gifts.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，命使調發朝鮮及野人女直兵會遼東，征北寇。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, winter, envoys were ordered to mobilize Korea and wild Jurchen troops to assemble at Liaodong and campaign against the northern raiders.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, winter, envoys were ordered to mobilize Korean and wild Jurchen troops to assemble at Liaodong and campaign against the northern raiders.

sentences.zh: 時英宗北狩，郕王即位，遣官頒詔于其國。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Yingzong was on the northern hunt; the Prince of Cheng established himself and dispatched officials to promulgate an edict in that state.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Yingzong was on the northern hunt; the Prince of Cheng established himself and dispatched officials to promulgate an edict in that state.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年貢馬五百匹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, five hundred tribute horses were offered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai, five hundred tribute horses were offered.

sentences.zh: 奏稱奉敕辦馬二三萬匹，比因鄰寇構釁，馬畜踣斃，一時未能。

translations.literal: The memorial stated that by imperial instruction they were to supply twenty or thirty thousand horses; recently because neighboring raiders had provoked incidents, horses and livestock had fallen and died, and they could not do so for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial stated that by imperial instruction they were to supply twenty or thirty thousand horses; recently, because neighboring raiders had provoked incidents, horses and livestock had fallen and died, and they could not do so for the moment.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「寇今少息。

translations.literal: An edict said: The raiders have now somewhat subsided.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The raiders have now somewhat subsided.

sentences.zh: 馬已至者，償其直。

translations.literal: For horses already arrived, pay their price.
translations.idiomatic: For horses already arrived, pay their price.

sentences.zh: 未至者，止勿貢。

translations.literal: For those not yet arrived, cease—do not offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: For those not yet arrived, cease—do not offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 」是年夏，祹卒，賜弔祭，諡莊憲，封子珦為國王。

translations.literal: That summer Do died; condolences and sacrifices were granted; the posthumous title Zhuangxian was bestowed and his son Gyeong was invested as king.
translations.idiomatic: "That summer Do died; condolences and sacrifices were granted, the posthumous title Zhuangxian was bestowed, and his son Gyeong was invested as king.

sentences.zh: 會遼東奏報開原、瀋陽有寇入境，掠人畜，系建州、海西、野人女直頭目李滿住等為嚮導，因諭珦相為掎角截殺之。

translations.literal: Just then Liaodong reported that raiders had entered Kaiyuan and Shenyang, looting people and livestock, with the Jianzhou, Haixi, and wild Jurchen chieftains Li Manju and others serving as guides; thereupon Gyeong was instructed to cooperate in pincer attacks to intercept and destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Liaodong reported that raiders had entered Kaiyuan and Shenyang, looting people and livestock, with Jianzhou, Haixi, and wild Jurchen chieftains Li Manju and others serving as guides; Gyeong was therefore instructed to cooperate in pincer attacks to intercept and destroy them.

sentences.zh: 其秋，續貢馬千五百餘匹。

translations.literal: That autumn more than one thousand five hundred additional tribute horses were offered.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn more than fifteen hundred additional tribute horses were offered.

sentences.zh: 賜冕服，並償其直。

translations.literal: Court robes were granted and their price paid.
translations.idiomatic: Court robes were granted and payment was made for the horses.

sentences.zh: 冬又賜珦及妃權氏誥命，封其子弘為世子。

translations.literal: In winter again patents of appointment were granted to Gyeong and his consort Lady Quan, investing his son Hong-wi as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In winter patents of appointment were again granted to Gyeong and his consort Lady Quan, investing his son Hong-wi as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，以建州頭目潛與朝鮮通，戒珦絕其使。

translations.literal: In the second year, winter, because Jianzhou chieftains had secretly communicated with Korea, Gyeong was warned to cut off their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, winter, because Jianzhou chieftains had secretly communicated with Korea, Gyeong was warned to cut off relations with them.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，珦卒，來告哀。

translations.literal: In the third year, autumn, Gyeong died; envoys came to report mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, autumn, Gyeong died, and envoys came to report mourning.

sentences.zh: 遣中官往弔祭，賜諡恭順，命子弘嗣立。

translations.literal: Palace eunuchs were dispatched to offer condolences and sacrifices; the posthumous title Gongshun was granted; his son Hong-wi was ordered to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs were dispatched to offer condolences and sacrifices; the posthumous title Gongshun was granted, and his son Hong-wi was ordered to succeed.

sentences.zh: 弘立三年，以年幼且嬰夙疾，請以叔瑈權國事。

translations.literal: Hong-wi had reigned three years; being young and afflicted with chronic illness since infancy, he requested his uncle Yu manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hong-wi had reigned three years; being young and afflicted with chronic illness since infancy, he requested that his uncle Yu manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 七年上表遜位，乃封瑈為國王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he presented a memorial abdicating; thereupon Yu was invested as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he presented a memorial abdicating, and Yu was thereupon invested as king.

sentences.zh: 瑈請立子暲為世子，從之。

translations.literal: Yu requested to establish his son Yeong as heir apparent; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yu requested to establish his son Yeong as heir apparent, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 天順三年，邊將奏，有建州三衛都督私與朝鮮結，恐為中國患。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshun, border generals memorialized that commanders of the three Jianzhou guards had privately allied with Korea, fearing they would become a calamity for China.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianshun, border generals reported that commanders of the three Jianzhou guards had privately allied with Korea, fearing this would become a calamity for China.

sentences.zh: 因敕瑈毋作不靖，貽後悔。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yu was instructed not to act unruly, lest he bring later regret.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was thereupon instructed not to act unruly, lest he bring later regret.

sentences.zh: 瑈疏辨，復諭曰：「宣德、正統年間，以王國與彼互相侵掠，敕解怨息兵，初不令交通給賞授官也。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a memorial in defense; he was again instructed: During the Xuande and Zhengtong reigns, because your kingdom and they mutually raided one another, an instruction was issued to resolve enmity and cease arms—it did not permit communication, granting rewards, or conferring office.
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted a memorial in defense; he was again instructed, "During the Xuande and Zhengtong reigns, because your kingdom and they mutually raided one another, an instruction was issued to resolve enmity and cease arms—it did not permit communication, granting rewards, or conferring office.

sentences.zh: 彼既受朝廷官職，王又加之，是與朝廷抗也。

translations.literal: Since they have already received offices from the court, and the king adds to them—this is opposing the court.
translations.idiomatic: Since they have already received offices from the court, and the king adds to them, this is opposing the court.

sentences.zh: 王素秉禮義，何爾文過飾非？

translations.literal: The king has always upheld ritual and righteousness—why do you now gloss over faults and conceal wrongs?
translations.idiomatic: You have always upheld ritual and righteousness—why do you now gloss over your faults and conceal your wrongs?

sentences.zh: 後宜絕私交，以全令譽。

translations.literal: Hereafter you should cut off private relations, to preserve your fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth you should sever private ties, so as to preserve your good reputation."

sentences.zh: 」四年復諭瑈曰：「王奏毛憐衛都督郎卜兒哈通謀煽亂，已置之法。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Yu was again instructed: The king memorialized that Maolin Guard Commander Langbu'erha conspired to incite rebellion, and he has been executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Yu was again instructed: "You memorialized that Maolin Guard Commander Langbu'erha conspired to incite rebellion, and he has been executed according to law.

sentences.zh: 夫法止可行于國中，豈得加於鄰境。

translations.literal: Now, law may be applied only within one's own state—how can it be imposed on neighboring territory?
translations.idiomatic: Law may be applied only within one's own state—how can it be imposed on neighboring territory?

sentences.zh: 郎卜兒哈有罪，宜奏朝廷區處。

translations.literal: If Langbu'erha had committed a crime, you should have memorialized the court for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: If Langbu'erha had committed a crime, you should have memorialized the court to handle the matter.

sentences.zh: 今輒行殺害，何怪其子阿比車之思復仇也。

translations.literal: Now you rashly carried out killing—why wonder that his son Abiche thinks of revenge?
translations.idiomatic: Now you rashly carried out the killing—no wonder his son Abiche seeks revenge.

sentences.zh: 聞阿比車之母尚在，宜急送遼東都司，令阿比車領回，以解仇怨。

translations.literal: It is heard that Abiche's mother is still alive; you should promptly send her to the Liaodong regional command, let Abiche take her back, to resolve enmity.
translations.idiomatic: We hear that Abiche's mother is still alive. You should promptly send her to the Liaodong regional command and let Abiche take her back, so as to resolve the feud."

sentences.zh: 」五年，建州衛野人至義州殺掠，瑈奏乞朝命還所掠。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Jianzhou Guard wild Jurchen came to Yizhou to kill_blk and plunder; Yu memorialized begging a court order to return what was plundered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Jianzhou wild Jurchen raided Yizhou, killing and plundering. Yu memorialized, requesting a court order for the return of plundered goods.

sentences.zh: 兵部議：「朝鮮先嘗誘殺郎卜兒哈，繼又誘致都指揮兀克，縱兵掠其家屬。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War deliberated: Korea first lured and killed Langbu'erha, then lured Battalion Commander Wuke, and unleashed troops to plunder his family.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War deliberated: "Korea first lured Langbu'erha to his death, then lured Battalion Commander Wuke and unleashed troops to plunder his household.

sentences.zh: 今野人實系復仇，宜諭朝鮮，寇盜之來皆自取，惟守分安法，庶弭邊釁。

translations.literal: Now the wild Jurchen are in fact seeking revenge; Korea should be instructed that raiders come through their own doing; only by keeping bounds and observing law can border troubles be quelled.
translations.idiomatic: The wild Jurchen are in fact seeking revenge. Korea should be told that these raids are of its own making, and that only by keeping within its bounds and observing the law can border troubles be quelled."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 成化元年冬，陪臣李門炯來朝，卒於道。

translations.literal: In winter of the first year of Chenghua, the envoy Li Menjiong came to court and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Chenghua, the Korean envoy Li Menjiong came to court but died en route.

sentences.zh: 命給棺賜祭，並賜彩幣慰其家。

translations.literal: An order was given to provide a coffin and grant sacrifices; colored silks were also bestowed to comfort his family.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a coffin and sacrificial offerings, and colored silks were also bestowed to comfort his family.

sentences.zh: 時朝鮮頻貢異物，三年春，敕諭瑈修常貢，勿事珍奇。

translations.literal: At that time Korea frequently offered exotic tribute; in spring of the third year an instruction admonished Yu to restore regular tribute and not indulge in rarities.
translations.idiomatic: Korea was then frequently sending exotic tribute items. In the spring of the third year an instruction admonished Yu to keep to regular tribute and not indulge in rare curiosities.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷用兵征建州，敕瑈助兵進剿。

translations.literal: At that time the court raised arms to campaign against Jianzhou and instructed Yu to aid troops in advance suppression.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the court was campaigning against Jianzhou and instructed Yu to assist the troops in the punitive advance.

sentences.zh: 瑈遣中樞府知事康純統眾萬餘渡鴨綠、潑豬二江，攻破九獮府諸寨，斬獲多。

translations.literal: Yu sent Secretariat Director Kang Chun leading more than ten thousand men across the Yalu and Pozhu Rivers, stormed the stockades of Jiun Prefecture, and decapitations and captures were many.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Kang Chun, Director of the Secretariat, at the head of more than ten thousand men across the Yalu and Pozhu Rivers. They stormed the stockades of Jiun Prefecture and took many heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 四年正月遣官來獻俘。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year officials were sent to present captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year envoys were sent to present captives.

sentences.zh: 詔從厚賚，敕獎諭之。

translations.literal: An edict granted generous rewards; an instruction praised and commended them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted generous rewards, and an instruction praised and commended them.

sentences.zh: 是年，瑈卒，賜諡惠莊。

translations.literal: That year Yu died; the posthumous title Huizhuang was granted.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yu died and was granted the posthumous title Huizhuang.

sentences.zh: 遣太監鄭同、崔安封世子晄為王，給妃韓氏誥命。

translations.literal: Eunuchs Zheng Tong and Cui An were dispatched to invest heir apparent Gwang as king and grant patent of appointment to consort Lady Han.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Zheng Tong and Cui An were dispatched to invest heir apparent Gwang as king, and patent of appointment was granted to his consort Lady Han.

sentences.zh: 既行，巡按遼東御史侯英奏曰：「遼東連年被寇，瘡痍未起，今復禾稼不登，軍民乏食。

translations.literal: After they had set out, the touring censor of Liaodong Hou Ying memorialized: Liaodong has been raided year after year; wounds are not healed; now crops again fail and soldiers and people lack food.
translations.idiomatic: After they had set out, Hou Ying, the touring censor of Liaodong, memorialized: "Liaodong has been raided year after year; it has not yet recovered from the devastation, crops have again failed, and soldiers and civilians alike lack food.

sentences.zh: 太監鄭同等隨從人員所過驛騷。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Zheng Tong and others with their retinues disturbed the relay stations wherever they passed.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the eunuchs Zheng Tong and the others passed with their retinues, they disturbed the relay stations.

sentences.zh: 臣考先年曾于翰林院中，選有學行文望者出使。

translations.literal: Your subject finds that in former years men of learning, literary attainment, and reputation were selected from the Hanlin Academy to serve as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject notes that in former years men of learning, literary attainment, and standing were selected from the Hanlin Academy to serve as envoys abroad.

sentences.zh: 今同、安俱朝鮮人，墳墓宗族皆在，見其國王，不免屈節，殊褻中國體。

translations.literal: Now Tong and An are both Koreans; their graves and clans are all there; meeting their king, they cannot but abase themselves—greatly debasing China's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tong and Cui An are both Koreans; their ancestral graves and clans are all there. In audience with the Korean king they cannot but demean themselves—grievously compromising the dignity of the empire.

sentences.zh: 乞寢成命，或翰林，或給事中及行人內推選一員，往使為便。

translations.literal: I beg that the completed order be withdrawn; or from among the Hanlin Academy, supervising secretaries, or heralds one might be selected to go as envoy, which would be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the present appointment be revoked and that one be selected instead from the Hanlin Academy, the supervising secretaries, or the heralds—this would be far more appropriate for such a mission."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「英所言良是。

translations.literal: The emperor said: What Ying said is quite correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What Hou Ying said is quite correct.

sentences.zh: 自後賞賚遣內臣，其冊封正副使，選廷臣有學行者。」

translations.literal: Henceforth for granting rewards envoys may be palace eunuchs; for chief and deputy investiture envoys, select court officials of learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth palace eunuchs may be sent to convey rewards, but chief and deputy investiture envoys shall be chosen from among court officials of learning and good conduct."

sentences.zh: 六年，晄病篤，以所生子幼，命其兄故世子暲女子娎子權國事，遣陪臣以聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Gwang fell gravely ill; because his born son was young, he ordered his elder brother the late heir apparent Yeong's daughter's son Hyeon to manage state affairs and sent envoys to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Gwang fell gravely ill. Because his own son was still young, he placed state affairs in the hands of Hyeon, son of his elder brother the late heir apparent Yeong's daughter, and sent envoys to report this to the court.

sentences.zh: 及卒，賜諡襄悼，命娎嗣位，娎妻韓氏封王妃。

translations.literal: When he died the posthumous title Xiangdao was granted; Hyeon was ordered to succeed; Hyeon's wife Lady Han was invested as queen consort.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was granted the posthumous title Xiangdao. Hyeon was ordered to succeed him, and Hyeon's wife Lady Han was invested as queen consort.

sentences.zh: 十年追贈娎父世子暲為國王，諡懷簡，母韓氏為王妃，從所請也。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Hyeon's father heir apparent Yeong was posthumously enfeoffed as king with posthumous title Huaijian, and his mother Lady Han as queen consort, as requested.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Hyeon's father, heir apparent Yeong, was posthumously enfeoffed as king and granted the posthumous title Huaijian; his mother Lady Han was posthumously invested as queen consort, as requested.

sentences.zh: 十一年四月，娎奏建州野人糾聚毛憐等衛侵擾邊境不已，乞朝命戒飭。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eleventh year Hyeon memorialized that Jianzhou wild Jurchen had gathered Maolin and other guards to harass the border without cease and begged a court order for restraint.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eleventh year Hyeon memorialized that Jianzhou wild Jurchen had gathered with Maolin and other guards to harass the border incessantly, and requested a court order for their restraint.

sentences.zh: 十二年十月，娎為繼妻尹氏請封，賜誥命冠服。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twelfth year Hyeon requested investiture for his second wife Lady Yun; patent of appointment, cap, and robes were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twelfth year Hyeon requested investiture for his second wife, Lady Yun; patent of appointment along with cap and robes were granted.
